newsitem.title: PANAMA: Telefonica knocked out of bid for Panama phone co.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica knocked out of bid for Panama phone co.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana SA was knocked out of the sale of Panama's state telephone utility INTEL, an INTEL spokesman said.
The National Telecommunications Institute board of directors "rejected the pre-qualification documents that Telefonica presented because it is a state-owned company," he said.
GTE Corp of the United States is so far the only company qualified to participate. A public bid is scheduled for early 1997.
Together with Telefonica, European firm Cable and Wireless Plc presented pre-qualification documents Tuesday to take part in the sale of 49 percent of INTEL.
Telefonica had withdrawn from the privatization process earlier this year after the Panamanian government decided to ban state-owned foreign corporations.
It was finally allowed in because the Spanish government's remaining 21 percent stake in Telefonica will be put up for sale next year. It was not clear why INTEL then decided to reject the bid.

The INTEL privatization went to a second round after the process was derailed when key bidder SBC Communications Inc pulled out, opting to participate in Brazil's more lucrative market, where at least 15 telecom sales are planned.
INTEL's value is estimated at $2 billion with assets of $450 million.
